Subject: High tail latency on streaming endpoint since 08:00 PDT

Hi Kim,

We're seeing a pronounced increase in tail latency for interactive streaming responses from the /v1/realtime endpoint starting ~08:00 PDT. Latency manifests as long pauses between streamed chunks (~6-12s) even when overall token rate is low. Impact: conversational UI stalls for several customers, some sessions time out.

Quick details:
- Model: rwd-base-1-8k (streaming)
- Region: us-west-2
- Customer traffic pattern: many short-turn conversations with prompt prefaces (~40 tokens) and ~100 token responses
- Example request id: orchard-req-20260509-8a7f

We opened an internal ticket but wanted to escalate — can you confirm whether this is on Redwood's side and suggest immediate workarounds? We can flip to non-streaming generation for affected users if needed.

Thanks,
Jared
Head of Product, OrchardAI
ops@orchardai.com

Jared — thanks for the signal and the request id. We're on it. I've opened RED-11893 and looped in SRE and product. Immediate items we're pushing now:

- Triage in progress (ben): collecting edge logs and token pacing traces.
- Short-term mitigation suggestions for your engineers (below) so you can reduce customer impact ASAP.
- We'll provide a replay of the logs and a follow-up postmortem by Tue.

Immediate recommended client-side mitigation (safe to do now):
1) Enable non-streaming fallback for the most affected traffic paths (call the same generation but without streaming). This avoids chunking gaps and usually reduces perceived stalls.
2) Set client-side stream timeout to 25s and show a reconnection prompt; this prevents user sessions hanging while we triage.
3) Reduce max_response_tokens to 120 for high-volume flows to shorten individual generation windows.
4) If you use the SDK, set streaming_chunk_size to 256 (instead of auto) to smooth pacing.

I'll let ben/engineering add any infra-side mitigations. Will update in 30–45m.

—Kim

Subject: Re: High tail latency on streaming endpoint — initial triage notes

Triage summary (observed 07:52–08:28 PDT):
- Symptom: intermittent token pacing pauses occurring on a subset of edge shards. Pauses look like JWT handshake latency + kernel-selection path that falls back to a slower attention kernel for sequences < 64 because of a mis-evaluated quantization heuristic.
- Trigger: request-burst pattern with many short conversations causing rapid KV cache churn on edge nodes. Autoscaler created new runtime pods which caused routing reshuffles; a small percentage of requests routed to pods with degraded token pacing.
- Scope: ~4% of traffic in us-west-2 during the window; amplified for workloads with short-turn prompts + many concurrent sessions.

Immediate infra actions taken (08:10–08:35):
- Applied routing pin (force-stick to warmed shards) for affected customer tags.
- Temporarily disabled the kernel heuristic that mis-selected the slow kernel (hotfix deployed at 08:22).
- Increased edge pod readiness grace to 45s to avoid premature routing to cold pods.

Recommended client mitigations to complement infra changes: (safe, low-risk)
- Flip to non-streaming for sessions that cannot tolerate pauses.
- Use max_response_tokens <= 120 where acceptable.
- If using SDK: enable prefix_kv_cache = true and set stream_chunk_size = 256.

I've uploaded a short log excerpt and the playbook to the ticket. We'll keep monitoring and report back in 1–2 hours.

—Ben
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 15:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-incident summary: OrchardAI interactive streaming slowdown (May 9)

Jared — thanks again for your patience and for hopping on the sync. Below is a concise post-incident summary and permanent recommendations. We appreciate the collaboration from your ops team.

Root cause (summary):
- A combination of (1) rapid KV-cache churn from short-turn conversation patterns and (2) an over-aggressive kernel-selection heuristic caused a small portion of requests to run on a slower attention kernel. This was amplified when the autoscaler spun up new pods, which briefly received traffic before cache warming completed, producing token pacing spikes.

What we did (timeline highlights):
- 07:52 PDT: elevated error/latency signals observed for a subset of us-west-2 shards.
- 08:10 PDT: SRE identified routing and kernel-selection correlation.
- 08:22 PDT: disabled heuristic via hotfix and applied routing pins to warmed shards.
- 08:35 PDT+: rollback of instances showing degraded pacing; monitoring confirmed improvement.

Customer impact:
- Affecting ~4% of OrchardAI requests during the window; user-visible stalls in interactive sessions for ~20–40 minutes for impacted sessions.

Permanent mitigations (what Redwood will do):
- Rework kernel-selection heuristic to factor in per-shard warm state and recent cache eviction metrics (in progress, target 2 weeks).
- Better autoscaler readiness gating to avoid early routing to cold pods (deployed immediate improvements; further tuning planned).
- Add a canary phase for kernel heuristics with traffic shaping (policy change).
- Provide a follow-up SDK release with safer streaming defaults (prefix_kv_cache enabled by default for short-turn workloads).

Recommended customer actions (best practices):
- Continue to prefer rwd-base-1-8k-dedicated for high-concurrency short-turn workloads.
- Set client-side stream timeout to 25–30s and have a retry fallback that issues a non-streaming call on timeout.
- Enable prefix_kv_cache in SDK and limit max_response_tokens to 120 for interactive flows where latency is critical.

Credits and next steps:
- We'll apply a one-time service credit for the affected window (details in support ticket RED-11893).
- Ben will share a short one-page technical brief to your SREs.
- Please let us know if you'd like a follow-up architecture review to optimize for your traffic profile.

Attachments: orchard_log_excerpt_20260509.txt, streaming-playbook-v1.2.pdf, postmortem-brief-20260512.docx

Thanks — we'll keep you informed as permanent fixes roll out.

—Kim
